_comment: Mutation testing config. Source of truth: GitHub #241. Mutates src/**/*.ts and runs tests/unit/**/*.test.ts only — see issue body for why we do not run integration or spec tests under Stryker (fileParallelism: false × Stryker concurrency races, plus mutation testing is a unit-test-shaped signal). Pinned to the 9.6.x line: vitest-runner@9.6.1 declares peer @stryker-mutator/core@9.6.1 and vitest >=2.0.0, which covers this repo's vitest@^4.0.0. We point Stryker at vitest.stryker.config.ts (a unit-only fork of vitest.config.ts) rather than the base config — Stryker's `vitest.dir` option filters against the resolved include pattern (which in the base config also picks up spec/) and `vitest.related` doesn't resolve our `../../src/foo.js` imports cleanly. See vitest.stryker.config.ts header for the full reasoning.
concurrency_comment: Default Stryker concurrency is fine for tests/unit/** — none of the unit tests share global state the way spec/npm-package and spec/fs-events do. If integration or spec tests are ever added to the runner scope, drop this to 1 (see issue #241 tradeoffs).
thresholds_comment: Advisory only for the first month, per the issue. Setting `break: 0` so Stryker never exits non-zero from a low score — the workflow keys issue-filing on survivor presence (via the script's exit code), not Stryker's score gate. Once we have a baseline number we can revisit.
